turns.question: Where is application-level route handling wired up, and is the router itself implemented inside this repository?
turns.text:
This confirms `router` is an external npm dependency (`^2.2.0`), not implemented in this repo. Let me check how application.js wires it up.Confirmed: `var Router = require('router');` in both files — imported from the external npm package, not a local module. Let me see exactly how the app wires it up (init, use, route methods).I have everything needed to answer confidently.

## Answer

**Application-level route handling is wired up in `lib/application.js`** (not in the `router` package itself). The key pieces:

- **`app.init`** (`lib/application.js:60-82`) lazily instantiates a `Router` instance on first access via a getter on `this.router`:
  ```js
  var Router = require('router');   // line 26
  ...
  router = new Router({ caseSensitive: ..., strict: ... });
  ```
- **`app.handle`** (`lib/application.js:~177`) dispatches every incoming request to it: `this.router.handle(req, res, done)`.
- **`app.use`** (`lib/application.js:190-244`) proxies to `router.use(path, fn)`, handling the special case of mounting a sub-app.
- **`app.route`** (`lib/application.js:256-258`) proxies to `this.router.route(path)`.
- **`app.param`** (`lib/application.js:331`) proxies to `this.router.param(name, fn)`.
- **HTTP verb methods** (`app.get`, `app.post`, etc.) are generated in a loop (`lib/application.js:470-482`) that calls `this.route(path)` and then invokes the verb on the returned `Route` object — again delegating to the router.
- **`lib/express.js`** re-exports the router's pieces as part of Express's public API: `exports.Route = Router.Route; exports.Router = Router;` (lines 70-71), and also does `var Router = require('router')` (line 19).

**Is the router implemented in this repo? No.** In both `lib/application.js` and `lib/express.js`, `Router` is obtained via `require('router')` — the separate npm package `router`, listed in `package.json` dependencies as `"router": "^2.2.0"`. There is no router implementation file inside `lib/` (the directory only contains `application.js`, `express.js`, `request.js`, `response.js`, `utils.js`, `view.js` — confirmed via `ghx tree`). Express's `lib/` only contains the **application wrapper** (settings, view rendering, request/response prototype extensions, and thin proxy methods) that delegates all actual path-matching/dispatch logic to the external `router` module.

**Not verified:** I did not fetch the source of the external `router` package itself (it lives in a separate repo, `expressjs/router`), so I can't describe its internal matching/dispatch implementation — only that Express's app layer delegates to it.

```js
import express from 'express'

app.get('/', (req, res) => {
  res.send('Hello World')
})

app.listen(3000, () => {
  console.log('Server is running on http://localhost:3000')
})
```

This is a [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/) module available through the
[npm registry](https://www.npmjs.com/).

Before installing, [download and install Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/download/).
Node.js 18 or higher is required.

If this is a brand new project, make sure to create a `package.json` first with
the [`npm init` command](https://docs.npmjs.com/creating-a-package-json-file).
